key_insight: The paper shows that an integrated modelling framework for liquid electrolyte design can be made more robust and extensible, with performance that improves across different systems and scales. It also reveals how training data size and composition influence how well the framework generalizes.
problem_solved: Designing liquid electrolytes is difficult because models often struggle to transfer across chemical systems and to remain reliable when data are limited or unevenly distributed.
method: Extended an existing unified framework for liquid electrolyte design to test its reusability and adaptability.
Evaluated how dataset size and composition affect model robustness and generalization.
Compared the framework against baseline approaches on cross-system transfer and multiscale performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights how to build scientific ML systems that are reusable rather than one-off models. It provides practical evidence that careful framework design can improve transferability and robustness in data-sparse materials design tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram of the integrated electrolyte-design framework
Bar chart comparing baseline vs. proposed framework on transferability and performance
Data-size sensitivity plot showing robustness as training data changes
Multiscale workflow graphic linking molecular, mesoscale, and system-level evaluation
paper_title: Reusability report: Exploring the utility and extensibility of an integrated modelling framework for liquid electrolyte design
paper_authors: Genming Lai, Juntao Zhao, Zekai Liu, Ruiqi Zhang, Hanming Li
